articles.title: Drishyam 3 Ends Overseas Run at Rs 144.89 Crore, Ninth-Biggest Bollywood Grosser Abroad Post-COVID
articles.excerpt: Ajay Devgn's crime thriller closed its international run as his biggest overseas grosser ever, with North America contributing an estimated $6.72 million, according to Koimoi's tracking.
articles.image_caption: A still from Drishyam 3, starring Ajay Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar. The film has ended its overseas run with an estimated Rs 144.89 crore gross, according to Koimoi.
articles.nri_angle: North America was the film's biggest overseas market — the diaspora audience made a Hindi thriller into a top-10 post-COVID international grosser.

articles.title: Simbu's 'Arasan' Promo Slips From Diwali to a Reported December 4 Theatre Release
articles.excerpt: The eight-minute 'World of Arasan' promo is finished except for Anirudh Ravichander's new background score, reports say, and the plan now is to attach it to Vijay Sethupathi's 'Train' in early December — reaching some 1,000 Tamil Nadu theatres instead of 100.
articles.image_caption: Director Vetrimaaran (left) with Silambarasan TR during the making of the Tamil film 'Arasan'. The film's eight-minute promo is now expected in theatres in December, reports say.
articles.nri_angle: The Arasan promo is planned for simultaneous theatrical and social-media release, so Tamil film fans in the US and elsewhere can expect to see it online the same day it reaches Tamil Nadu screens.

articles.title: 'Pyre': An 18-Award Himalayan Love Story Arrives in Cinemas With First-Time Actors
articles.excerpt: Vinod Kapri's Hindi drama casts two Uttarakhand villagers, aged 80 and 70, as a couple waiting 28 years for their son — and it has already collected 18 international awards, 15 of them for Best Film.
articles.image_caption: The poster for Pyre, written, directed and produced by Vinod Kapri, introducing Padam Singh and Heera Devi. The Hindi drama opened in Indian cinemas on October 30 after winning 18 international awards.
articles.nri_angle: A film about parents left behind in a Himalayan village waiting for a migrant son speaks directly to diaspora families; it is in Indian cinemas now, with no US release announced yet.

articles.title: Karan Johar Says He Is Dissuading Twins Yash And Roohi From Bollywood
articles.excerpt: On Koffee With Karan, the filmmaker said the industry is tough and he will be too old to protect his children when they are ready — a view Kareena Kapoor gently pushed back on.
articles.image_caption: Karan Johar poses against a red curtain backdrop. The filmmaker says he is dissuading his twins, Yash and Roohi, from joining Bollywood.
articles.nri_angle: A prominent diaspora-followed filmmaker questioning a Bollywood career for his own children speaks to wider debates about nepotism, scrutiny and parenting in the public eye.

articles.title: Drishyam 3 Ends BookMyShow Run As Bollywood's Tenth Highest Ticket-Seller Ever
articles.excerpt: The Hindi crime thriller starring Ajay Devgn sold 6.72 million tickets on BookMyShow in five weeks and closed with 379.65 crore net in India, becoming Devgn's highest ticket-selling film on the platform.
articles.image_caption: Drishyam
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans followed the concluding Hindi chapter overseas; the BookMyShow top-ten finish measures India platform ticket demand for a thriller-led franchise finale.

articles.title: Salman Khan Calls Maatrubhumi Rewrite Claims 'Nonsense' at Trailer Launch
articles.excerpt: The Hindi war drama, earlier titled Battle of Galwan, is 'a film on soldiers and their families on both sides,' the actor said — not an anti-China film, and not rewritten under government pressure.
articles.image_caption: Salman Khan at the Maatrubhumi trailer launch in Mumbai. He dismissed claims that the government pressured the makers to rewrite the film's script.
articles.nri_angle: Maatrubhumi is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 4 — diaspora audiences will find it in the usual North America Bollywood theatrical circuit.

articles.excerpt: The actor, who played Akshay Kumar's wife in the Hindi courtroom drama, says her name was dropped without explanation and a song featuring her was released without tagging her.

articles.title: Aishwarya and Abhishek Arrive Hand-in-Hand at Manish Malhotra's Diwali Bash

articles.title: Mookuthi Amman 2 Advance Sales Pass Nayanthara's Previous Opener
articles.excerpt: The Tamil fantasy sequel, releasing November 6 for Diwali, has Rs 1.26 crore in India advance sales, according to Koimoi — already above Hi's Rs 1.25 crore opening day, with a day of pre-sales left.
articles.image_caption: Nayanthara in her Mookuthi Amman 2 look, wearing a navy saree and nose ring in temple settings. The Tamil fantasy sequel releases in theatres worldwide on November 6, 2026, for Diwali.
articles.nri_angle: Tamil Diwali releases are a theatre ritual for the diaspora; the film opens worldwide November 6, with US showtimes to be checked locally.

articles.title: Ramayana Opens With Rs 42.96 Crore in Day 1 Advance Sales, Bollywood's Second-Best Ever
articles.excerpt: 12.14 lakh tickets sold before the first show, a record 26,615 shows, and the highest pre-sales ever for a non-sequel — the Ranbir Kapoor-Yash epic starts its run in the record books.
articles.image_caption: Ramayana
articles.nri_angle: Ramayana released worldwide the same day; North American pre-sales ran 106% higher than Adipurush per Koimoi's companion tracking, making this a diaspora opening weekend too.

articles.title: Anuv Jain Says Independent Music Lets Him Wait for Right Bollywood Project
articles.excerpt: The Ludhiana singer-songwriter told IANS he has had Bollywood offers but is 'quite selective,' crediting his independent releases for the financial and audience foundation that lets him choose his first film project carefully.
articles.nri_angle: Jain's sold-out London Roundhouse show and more than 20 million monthly Spotify listeners show that diaspora and streaming audiences can now sustain an Indian independent career without a Bollywood launch.

articles.title: Ramayana Part 2 Will Arrive in 2028, Producer Namit Malhotra Confirms
articles.excerpt: On the eve of Part 1 release on November 5, producer Namit Malhotra has confirmed the sequel moves from its planned Diwali 2027 window to 2028, saying the finale needs the extra year. The Hindi film is also being made in a separate English master version.
articles.image_caption: Producer Namit Malhotra and artwork from Ramayana, with Yash as Ravana above Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Malhotra has confirmed Part 2 will release in 2028 instead of 2027.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences, the English master version matters: Part 1 opens November 5 in two versions with different edits and runtimes, and Part 2 now lands in 2028.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At Ramayana's Mumbai Screening, Lakshman Ravi Dubey Seeks Hanuman Sunny Deol's Blessings
articles.excerpt: Dubey touched Deol's feet at the star-studded special screening on November 3 — a moment fans instantly framed as Lakshman honouring Hanuman, two days before the film's worldwide release.
articles.nri_angle: The defining image from the Mumbai screening of the diaspora's most anticipated Indian release of the season.

articles.title: Jailer 2 at Rs 816.9 Crore Closes In on Vijay's Tamil Nadu Record
articles.excerpt: Twenty days into its run, the Rajinikanth starrer needs about Rs 6.8 crore more in Tamil Nadu to pass 'The Greatest of All Time' — the last major record it has not yet taken.
articles.image_caption: Rajinikanth as retired jailer Tiger Muthuvel Pandian in a still from 'Jailer 2'. The film has collected Rs 816.90 crore worldwide in 20 days and is closing on the Tamil Nadu record held by Vijay's 'The Greatest of All Time'.
articles.nri_angle: The film's Rs 275.25 crore overseas gross — a Tamil cinema record — is powered substantially by diaspora audiences in the US, Gulf and Malaysia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi to Host Two-Day Diwali Festival With Drone Show at Central Park
articles.excerpt: 'Dilli Ki Diwali' brings a mega drone show, bhajan clubbing and competitions worth up to Rs 1.51 lakh to Connaught Place on November 6 and 7.
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's official open-air Diwali festival is the easiest celebration for diaspora families visiting the capital this week to attend.

articles.title: 'Kuch Toh Log Kahenge': Ranbir Kapoor Shrugs Off Ramayana Trolling Before Release
articles.excerpt: Days before Ramayana Part 1 opens in theatres, Ranbir Kapoor told 18,000 students that online trolling does not bother him and that the opinions of people who value his intentions matter most.
articles.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram in a still from Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, drawing a bow. Kapoor said this week that online trolling over the film does not bother him and that he values the people who trust his intentions.
articles.nri_angle: Ramayana Part 1 opens in theatres on November 5; diaspora audiences get Kapoor's own framing of the debate before opening weekend.

articles.title: Film Workers' Body Asks PM Modi for Foolproof Bollywood Security After Bachchan Shield
articles.excerpt: AICWA's appeal to the Prime Minister follows Amitabh Bachchan's bulletproof-glass Sunday greeting at Jalsa and a string of attacks on film personalities, from Baba Siddique's murder to the firing at Tiger Shroff.
articles.image_caption: Tiger Shroff, left, pictured with a bandage on his chest after the October firing in Juhu, and Amitabh Bachchan waving to fans from behind a protective enclosure at Jalsa. AICWA has cited both cases in its appeal to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for foolproof security for film personalities.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans, Bachchan's Sunday greeting at Jalsa is a decades-old ritual; its move behind bulletproof glass is the image driving Bollywood's security debate.

articles.title: Jailer 2 First Indian Film to Cross Rs 75 Crore in All Four South Markets
articles.excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel completed the milestone in Kerala on its 16th day, finishing a four-market run that eluded Baahubali 2, KGF Chapter 2 and Pushpa 2, according to Sacnilk.
articles.image_caption: Poster art for Jailer 2, with Rajinikanth flanked by Mohanlal and Shivarajkumar. The film crossed Rs 75 crore in each of the four major South Indian markets within 16 days, according to Sacnilk.
articles.nri_angle: Jailer 2's overseas gross of Rs 267.50 crore in 16 days, per Sacnilk, underlines the diaspora's weight in a Tamil blockbuster's economics.

articles.title: Ramayana Review: Critics Hail the Spectacle, Split on the Storytelling
articles.excerpt: Bollywood Hungama gave Nitesh Tiwari's Hindi epic a perfect 5/5, but international critics who saw the English dub ranged from IGN's 4/10 to Screen Rant's 7/10 — praising the scale, score and Yash's Ravana while faulting the pacing and crowding.
articles.image_caption: A still from Ramayana: Part 1 shows Rama standing before a waterfall. Critics praised the film's scale and spectacle while dividing on its storytelling.
articles.nri_angle: The film opens in US theatres on November 5 in both Hindi and English, and the split between Indian and international critics maps directly onto the choice diaspora viewers face between the original Hindi cut and the English dub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

critics.name: Taran Adarsh
critics.verdict: Ramayana is not merely a film; IT'S AN EXPERIENCE. It is a film that makes India proud.

critics.name: Christian Zilko
critics.verdict: Calling “Ramayana” epic may be a cliche, but there's really no other word that would suffice.

critics.name: Brandon Zachary
critics.verdict: On a purely visual and technical level, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is an impressive cinematic achievement.

critics.name: Giovanni Lago
critics.verdict: Audiences can still be swept up by “Ramayana,” even if it feels so stuffed at times that it might've needed a “Game of Thrones”-level television adaptation to flesh out its narrative fully.

critics.name: Siddhant Adlakha
critics.verdict: A majestic epic falls victim to clunky action, eye-sore CGI, and awkward AI lip-syncing in what is, unfortunately, just a Part 1.
